//PageSize: Page size for the [EnableQuery] collection reads, applied by ODataPageSizeConvention. An
action that names its own PageSize keeps it, and removing the key falls back to
ODataPageSizeConvention.FallbackPageSize. It must be 1 or greater: a value that would serve
these reads unpaged stops the host at startup rather than quietly removing the limit.

//EventEnvelopeSigning: Deliberately absent. This file ships to every environment, so a key here would silently
become the production signing key and remove the only alarm: EnvelopeIntegrityBroker
REFUSES TO CONSTRUCT without one, so every Core endpoint answers 500 rather than writing
rows it cannot announce. That is the fail-closed behaviour we want, and it has to happen at
construction — the broker used to defer it to the first publish, which lands after the write
has committed and strands the row it was refusing (#392). The host still starts and the SPA
still serves: InitializeCoreAsync logs the failure rather than halting, so check the log, not
the home page. A real value belongs in an environment variable or key
vault; a local development key belongs in appsettings.Development.json, which is
gitignored. Shape: EventEnvelopeSigning: [ { KeyId, Key, ActiveFrom, ActiveTo? } ].
